## Cheapest State Sales Tax Rates in the US (2026)

### States with Zero (0%) Sales Tax

The absolute cheapest sales tax is **0%**, found in **five states** — collectively known by the acronym **NOMAD**:

| State | State Sales Tax Rate | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| **New Hampshire** | 0% | No local sales tax either |
| **Oregon** | 0% | No local sales tax either |
| **Montana** | 0% | Some local resort taxes may apply |
| **Alaska** | 0% | Local jurisdictions may charge up to 7.5% |
| **Delaware** | 0% | No local sales tax either |

> **Note:** While these states charge **no state-level sales tax**, Alaska and Montana permit local governments to levy their own sales taxes. Delaware, New Hampshire, and Oregon have **no sales tax at any level**, making them the true lowest.

---

### Lowest Non-Zero State Sales Tax Rates

For states that **do** have a sales tax, the lowest rates are:

| State | State Sales Tax Rate |
|---|---|
| **Colorado** | 2.9% |
| **Alabama** | 4.0% |
| **Georgia** | 4.0% |
| **Hawaii** | 4.0% (General Excise Tax) |
| **New York** | 4.0% |
| **Wyoming** | 4.0% |

---

### Key Takeaway

**Delaware, New Hampshire, and Oregon** are the cheapest states for sales tax — charging **0% at both the state and local level**. If you are looking for the lowest non-zero state rate, **Colorado at 2.9%** holds that distinction.

> Keep in mind that **combined rates** (state + local) can differ significantly. For example, even in low-rate states like Alabama, local taxes can push the combined rate as high as **11%** in some jurisdictions.

*Sources: [Tax Foundation (2026)](https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/sales-tax-rates/), [Avalara (2026)](https://www.avalara.com/taxrates/en/state-rates.html)*

## Top 10 US States with the Lowest Sales Tax Rates (2026)

Here are the 10 states with the lowest **state-level** sales tax rates, ranked from lowest to highest, based on [Tax Foundation data as of January 1, 2026](https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/sales-tax-rates/):

| Rank | State | State Sales Tax Rate | Avg. Local Rate | Combined Rate |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Delaware** | 0.00% | 0.00% | **0.00%** |
| 1 | **Montana** | 0.00% | 0.00% | **0.00%** |
| 1 | **New Hampshire** | 0.00% | 0.00% | **0.00%** |
| 1 | **Oregon** | 0.00% | 0.00% | **0.00%** |
| 1 | **Alaska** | 0.00% | 1.82% | **1.82%** |
| 6 | **Colorado** | 2.90% | 4.99% | **7.89%** |
| 7 | **Alabama** | 4.00% | 5.46% | **9.46%** |
| 7 | **Georgia** | 4.00% | 3.49% | **7.49%** |
| 7 | **Hawaii** | 4.00% | 0.50% | **4.50%** |
| 7 | **New York** | 4.00% | 4.54% | **8.54%** |
| 7 | **Wyoming** | 4.00% | 1.56% | **5.56%** |

> **Note:** There is a tie at rank 7, giving 11 states in the top 10 by state rate. The table includes all tied states for completeness.

### Key Observations

**Delaware, Montana, New Hampshire, and Oregon** charge absolutely **no sales tax** at either the state or local level, making them the clear winners for lowest overall tax burden on purchases.

**Alaska** also has a 0% state rate, but local governments can levy up to **7.85%**, resulting in an average combined rate of 1.82%.

**Colorado** holds the title of the **lowest non-zero state sales tax** at just **2.9%**, though its high average local rate of 4.99% pushes the combined rate to 7.89%.

**Hawaii** is notable among the 4% states — its low average local rate of just 0.50% gives it the **lowest combined rate (4.50%)** among all states that actually levy a sales tax, making it the most affordable taxed state overall.

*Source: [Tax Foundation — State and Local Sales Tax Rates, 2026](https://taxfoundation.org/data/all/state/sales-tax-rates/)*
